h: Quickmart NSE listing still awaits regulator approval, with no offer price set
s: Adenia's Sokoni Retail plans to sell a 50% stake (2bn shares) on the NSE. Analysts value the company at KES 25.5–34bn. The seller wants the offer open around 30 Sep, but the CMA and NSE have not approved it yet.
opp: PE exit with no primary capital; benchmark the price against regional grocers.

h: SARB raises repo rate 25bp to 7.25% as oil shock persists
s: The Reserve Bank hiked, citing Middle East-driven fuel prices and rising global rates.
opp: Reprice SAGB curve and rate-sensitives (retail, REITs); watch USD/ZAR into 4 Nov elections.

h: Airtel Money plans London IPO, with IFC as cornerstone investor
s: The mobile-money unit (about 53m monthly users across 13 markets) plans to float at least 10% on the LSE. IFC will invest up to $90m, with pricing expected mid-October.
opp: Sum-of-the-parts re-rating of AAF; compare with M-Pesa and MoMo multiples.

h: Bank of Ghana MPC meets as inflation rises to 5% and cedi weakens
s: Policy rate has been 14% since July. August CPI rose to 5.0%, and the cedi is weakening again as gold FX inflows soften.
opp: Easing cycle may pause; position in short GoGs and cedi forwards.

h: GoldBod purchase freeze since mid-August threatens Ghana's reserve rebuild
s: Physical gold reserves were 24.4t in June, down 26% y/y. With no restart date, a ~$1.4bn September FX mandate is at risk.
opp: Cedi downside risk rises; hedge GHS exposure.

h: Egypt's central bank expected to hold rates a fifth time as core inflation rises
s: Deposit rate is 19% and lending rate 20%. Headline CPI eased to 14.5%, but core rose to 14.9%.
opp: T-bill real yields stay high; carry depends on a stable EGP.

h: NGX market cap hits record N163tn on FTSE-driven buying
s: The ASI kept climbing, even as investors sold other stocks to fund Dangote IPO subscriptions.
opp: Momentum is strong; watch for liquidity to drain into the IPO before it closes 13 Oct.

h: CBN cuts policy rate 350bp to 23% and keeps cash reserve ratio at 45%
s: The MPR fell from 26.5% to 23%, with the corridor at +50/−300bp. Banks' cash reserve ratio stays at 45%.
opp: Duration in FGN bonds and T-bills benefits; the high CRR caps bank margins.

h: Mozambique pitches its $50bn Rovuma LNG portfolio to Brazilian investors
s: Mozambique LNG restarted in January and targets first output in 2029. Exxon's Rovuma LNG aims for a final investment decision in 2026. State firm ENH gets a 15% free carry.
opp: Rovuma investment decision is the catalyst for services firms and Mozambique sovereign credit.

h: Nigeria returns to FTSE Frontier as the ASI tops 250,000 (+60.8% YTD)
s: The reclassification took effect 21 Sep and is expected to bring $0.8–1bn of passive inflows.
opp: Trade passive flows into the large-cap additions; watch for a fade once buying ends.

h: Strike notices at Barrick's Loulo-Gounkoto mine in Mali put gold guidance at risk
s: Strikes are called for 28 Sep–2 Oct. The complex needs a strong H2 to meet 260–290koz guidance.
opp: Pair Barrick against West African gold peers.

h: MNT-Halan's Egyptian arm lines up a large EGX main-board IPO
s: MNT Tech has held roadshows in the Gulf, London and the US ahead of Egypt's biggest fintech listing.
opp: Could draw foreign money back to the EGX; compare its valuation with Fawry.

h: Ethiopian Securities Exchange approves 11 new listings
s: The young exchange has cleared a large expansion of its equity market.
opp: Early frontier market; watch the listing pipeline and foreign-access rules.

h: YW Capital and RMB close a R2.25bn Pepkor logistics property deal
s: A sale-and-leaseback through the IronOak platform frees capital for Pepkor.
opp: Watch for more SA retailers selling property to free up capital.

h: Dangote refinery opens N2.15tn IPO, billed as Africa's biggest
s: The $1.6bn offer is priced at N525 a share and closes 13 Oct. At listing it could be 25–30% of NGX cap.
opp: Index-weight shock and investors selling other stocks to fund bids; plan for inclusion flows.

h: Senegal plans a $5bn debt 'treatment' and pays its Eurobond coupon
s: IMF staff agreed a $2.2bn programme on 1 Sep. Senegal seeks G20 help to reprofile commercial debt, and bondholders have organised.
opp: Distressed funds may position before the terms are set.

h: Nigeria's crude output reaches 1.68m b/d, meeting its OPEC quota a fourth month
s: August output rose 0.4% after the Erha loading buoy was fixed.
opp: Supports FX reserves, the naira and Lagos-listed oil stocks.

h: Lobito railway aims to double minerals cargo in 2027 after a $300m drawdown
s: About 400kt of international cargo is expected in 2026, after a record 27kt in July.
opp: Lowers export costs for Copperbelt producers.

h: EIA raises H2 2026 Brent forecast to about $90 on Middle East shut-ins
s: About 6.7m b/d was shut in during August. The EIA expects $74 in 2027 as disruption eases.
opp: Exporters (NG, AO) benefit; importers (KE, SA, EG) suffer on FX and inflation.

h: Angola weighs a Eurobond return as a tight election approaches
s: A new dollar bond is under consideration as political tension builds.
opp: New supply could pressure the curve; weigh it against oil and election risk.

h: Angola approves the sale of 34% of Standard Bank Angola via BODIVA
s: The state sells up to about $261m. Standard Bank Group's stake rises to 75% and the public gets 10%. Trading starts 30 Sep.
opp: Tests Angola's privatisation drive and BODIVA liquidity.

h: African startups raised $438m in August, with over 90% going to Moove and Jumia
s: Year-to-date funding reached about $2.1bn while early-stage rounds fell.
opp: Room for secondaries and well-funded early-stage investors.

h: BRVM sustainability bond programme targets XOF 90bn
s: Issuers are Baobab CI and Senegal (6.80%, 5 years) and Shelter Afrique (6.10–6.30%), running through October.
opp: Euro-pegged local ESG paper versus WAEMU sovereigns.

h: Casablanca's MASI gained 4.5% in August and Managem is now the largest listed company
s: Managem rose 31% in August; brokers see September as a stock-picker's market.
opp: Precious-metals exposure inside Morocco.

h: Zimbabwe's ZiG holds near 26/$ as inflation falls to 2.9%
s: Reserves are above $1.5bn and H1 gold exports were about $3.1bn. The parallel premium is about 20%.
opp: The parallel gap signals conversion risk for ZSE holders.

h: AngloGold jumped 41.6% in August on higher profit and a $2bn buyback
s: Q2 profit rose 58%, and it led gold miners in August.
opp: High sensitivity to the bullion price; track the buyback pace.

h: JSE regains 116k as gold and PGM miners rally and Naspers lags
s: Gold miners rose 38% and PGM miners 21.6% in August, while Naspers and Prosus fell with Chinese tech.
opp: Rotate from Naspers/Prosus into miners.

h: Ethiopian birr at 161/$ with a wide parallel premium and 15.3% inflation
s: The birr is down about 12.6% y/y, with bureau rates near 177. IMF has disbursed $2.65bn of $3.4bn.
opp: FX convergence drives Eurobond recovery values and ESX entry.

h: CDG Invest and Mediterrania Capital back Moroccan water firm SNCE
s: Joint acquisition in water infrastructure.
opp: Water scarcity is becoming an investable North African theme.

h: Continental Re plans Botswana's first IPO since 2017 (~$156m)
s: The P2.1bn raise, P1.7bn of it primary, is priced at 1.21× book and lists 5 Oct.
opp: Rare listed pan-African reinsurer, with NGN and KES exposure.

h: Côte d'Ivoire sets cocoa farmgate price at 1,200 CFA/kg, down 57%
s: StoneX sees output falling 11% to 1.77mt on fertiliser costs and El Niño risk.
opp: Supply risk on the cocoa futures curve; watch smuggling to Ghana.

h: CBK approves Nedbank's $842m takeover of 66% of NCBA
s: Payment is 80% shares and 20% cash, and the CMA waived a mandatory offer. Completion is expected in October.
opp: Merger-arbitrage spread into completion.

h: Ghana requires local refining of artisanal gold doré from 1 Sep
s: GoldBod will clear exports only after in-country refining; 104t was shipped in 2025.
opp: Local refiners gain; near-term FX inflows could slip.

h: MTN reports a record H1 margin, launches a R6bn buyback, and nears closing the IHS deal
s: Service revenue rose 17.5% in constant currency and EBITDA about 25%.
opp: Buyback support, plus scope to surface the value of MoMo.

h: AfDB approves $255m for Zambia's section of the Lobito corridor
s: Funds 550km of new rail linking the Copperbelt to Lobito port.
opp: Lowers execution risk on the corridor.

h: A.P. Moller Capital to buy a majority stake in Morocco's Globex
s: The infrastructure fund is taking control of the logistics group.
opp: Nearshoring is driving consolidation of port-linked assets.

h: Airtel and Starlink launch Africa's first satellite-to-phone service in DRC
s: Standard Android phones can now connect directly for messaging and light data.
opp: Direct-to-phone satellite service challenges tower-company growth assumptions.

h: Namibia's Venus oil final investment decision slips to late 2026
s: TotalEnergies cites gas content and fiscal terms; first oil is expected in 2029.
opp: Delays Namibia's fiscal upside; sets a precedent for the Orange Basin.

h: Jumia raises $50m equity from IFC and Axian
s: Funds the path to profitability.
opp: Backing from a development lender lowers funding risk.

h: DRC holds its cobalt export cap at 87kt and warns of cuts if prices fall
s: Cobalt slid to $22–23/lb on weak Chinese battery demand.
opp: A quota cut would push cobalt prices sharply higher.

h: CBK holds Kenya's policy rate at 8.75%; reserves at $15.2bn
s: Inflation is inside the target band, the shilling is stable, and private credit growth is 10.2%.
opp: Favour short-dated Kenyan paper over long.

h: Zambia's copper concentrate duty waiver ends 30 Sep
s: The 10% duty returns; about 272kt had been exempted while smelters were under maintenance.
opp: Watch for an extension; miners' margins depend on it.

h: Moove raises $250m Series C at a $2.1bn valuation, led by Mubadala
s: Funds fleet infrastructure for autonomous mobility.
opp: Gulf sovereign money is backing African-founded platforms.

h: Yellow Card raises $40m for stablecoin payment rails
s: Backers include SC Ventures and Sony Innovation Fund.
opp: Stablecoin rails compete with correspondent-banking fees.
